question: Which of the following was a Ceylonese chronicle that acted as an important literary source of the Mauryan empire?
solution:
The Correct Answer is**Mahavamsa.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The **Mahavamsa** is an important** Ceylonese (Sri Lankan)** chronicle written in Pali.
 
• It provides a** continuous historical record **of over two millennia.
 
• It is a key source for the understanding of the history of not only Sri Lanka but also the Indian subcontinent, **especially during the Mauryan empire.**
 
• The chronicle covers the early history of Buddhism in Sri Lanka and the interactions between the rulers of Sri Lanka and the Mauryan Empire.
 
• It is considered one of the **world's longest-unbroken **historical accounts and has been crucial in constructing the history of the region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
 

 Option
 Details
 
 

 1) Indica
 Written by Megasthenes, the Greek ambassador to the Mauryan court, Indica is an account of his observations of India and its people.
 
 

 2) Mudrarakshas
 A Sanskrit play by Vishakhadatta that depicts the ascent of the Mauryan Emperor Chandragupta Maurya to power.
 
 

 4) Arthashastra
 Attributed to Chanakya (Kautilya), it is an ancient Indian treatise on statecraft, economic policy, and military strategy.
